newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK overnight rate surges on month-end, stock run.
newsitem.headline: HK overnight rate surges on month-end, stock run.

text.p: Hong Kong's overnight cash rate jumped more than one percentage point on Friday on active borrowing from banks for month-end and equities-related demand, despite an injection by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, dealers said.
"Overnight was still offered at six percent at noon after the HKMA's HK$1.0 billion injection," a local bank dealer said.
Overnight cash surged to a high of 6-1/4 before settling at 6 5-7/8 percent, against five 4-7/8 percent at Thursday midday.
An HKMA executive said the injection was aimed at soothing the tightness in the interbank market, but dealers speculated it might need a second go in the afternoon.
"The market is still tight after the injection," one dealer said.

Market talks said China property and hotel investor Nam Fong International Holdings Ltd's public offer of 68 million shares was seen more than 150 times subscribed. The offer closed at noon on Friday.
Longer-term cash also rose with three-month at 5-11/16 1/2 percent against 5-1/2 7/16.
In the government paper market, trading was hectic with activity focused on short-dated bills, dealers said.
"The market was a bit chaotic at the opening as the overnight surged so high and nobody was sure what levels short-term bills should trade," one dealer said.
The one-week bill yield jumped to 5.13 percent from 4.64 on Thursday and one-month yielded 4.69 versus 4.64.
Trading on longer-dated paper was steady since with no guidance from the U.S. market, which was on holiday on Thursday.
Three-year notes yielded 5.98 percent versus 6.00, the seven-year yielded 6.86 versus 6.87 and the 10-year was 7.10 versus 7.11.
